# The harnesses

Generated 2026-10-29 by `ham.citybuildersim.tools.HarnessMap` - every labelled assertion in every harness, under the section it prints. Do not edit; regenerate with `Regenerate maps.bat`.

> bytes and text.

## HomeRailCheck.java - 45 labelled assertions

> The railway's carriage of the city's own bulk, and the port yard, held to FR6's
> brief: a bulk tonne bought at home rides a siding at the city leg's rate on
> the room the boundary's tonnes leave, a tonne that crossed a berth rides the
> port yard's rails to the same rule, and every leg is billed once.
> 
> WHY THIS HARNESS EXISTS. Until FR6 the railway was offered only what crossed
> the boundary: the ore from a city's mine to its own mill was a whole truck leg
> at Haulage's quote though FR7 lays the mine a siding, and a tonne landed at a
> berth was a whole truck leg from the quay to the door. FR6 (docs/queue/FR6.md)
> deals those tonnes to the railway last, after the boundary's, bills them at the
> railway's quote on Haulage's, and takes their railed part off the trucks' leg.

> ...

## LandClassCheck.java - 159 labelled assertions

> A price for each class of ground, checked (ET3, slice A; docs/studies/spec-earth2-terrain.md 5.1 and 5.2): the going
> price stays the price of flat ground, foothill is that price less its preparation and never under the base price of
> unwanted ground, steep and very steep ground is the base price - no class dearer than flat. The land office prices
> its offers by the ground they hold, the pickers rank them by the ground a building can stand on with its preparation
> counted, and a business pays the city for its plot class by class.
> 
> WHAT THIS HAS TO PROVE, every fixture causing the condition it tests and every figure worked out from the model's own
> constants and getters (LandMarket.openingUsdPerSqFt(), SitePreparation, LandManager's square feet) and never typed:
> 
>   1. THE RULE. LandMarket.reliefPrice() for each class with the going price above the base plus the preparation
>      (foothill = going less the preparation), between the base and base plus the preparation (foothill = base) and

> the ring a one-for-one strike let run echoes less; a save carries the struck

## SaveFileCheck.java - 608 labelled assertions

> Verifies where saves go and how they are written.
> 
> This is the only part of the game where a bug destroys something the player
> cannot get back. Everything else can be re-simulated; a save written over
> badly is a city that no longer exists. So the tests here are deliberately
> mean: they fill the target with junk, point the writer at a path it cannot
> write to, and check that in every case the file that was already on disk is
> still exactly what it was.
> 
> Path resolution is tested through the pure resolveDirectory() rather than the
> real environment, because a chooser that reads System.getenv can only be
> tested on the machine it is running on - which is precisely the machine where
> ...
